status: generated by tools/build_taxonomy.py from explicit rules
note: A SECOND INDEX over the mechanics. Nothing here alters, renames or reinterprets Rosewater's mechanic, tier or explanation. Families are Vox Mana navigation vocabulary and must be labelled as such wherever shown. There is deliberately no miscellaneous family.

rules.primary_family: exactly one; first matching rule wins
rules.secondary_families: zero or more; all matching rules apply
rules.never: a family may not become a mechanic's canonical identity, and may not feed backward into tier, colour or label

families.removal: answering a permanent already on the battlefield
families.card_flow: drawing, filtering, looting, scrying - moving cards through hand and library
families.tutoring: searching the library for a named or typed card
families.mana: producing, fixing, ramping or untapping mana sources
families.graveyard: using the graveyard as a resource, or denying it
families.tokens: creating creatures or artifacts from nothing
families.combat: how creatures fight once they are on the battlefield
families.evasion: making a creature hard or impossible to block
families.protection: keeping your own things alive, untargetable or uncounterable
families.disruption: attacking the opponent's hand, library or resources
families.control: stopping things before or as they happen
families.copying: duplicating a permanent or a spell
families.theft: taking control of something the opponent owns
families.sacrifice: converting your own resources - permanents, cards, life - into another
families.life: life total as a resource - gaining, draining, paying
families.tempo: buying or stealing time - bouncing, untapping, extra turns
families.rules_alteration: changing how the game itself works
families.card_type_affinity: caring that a particular card type is present
families.stat_modification: changing a creature's printed power or toughness
families.cheat_into_play: putting cards onto the battlefield without paying their cost
families.characteristic_change: changing what something IS - its colour, its types, or the words printed on it, as distinct from its size
families.win_condition: altering how the game is won or lost
